## 7. Runtime verification: a clean dogfood probe

The `verifier` agent prompt is the strongest epistemic artifact in the harness. It requires inline citations, URL resolution, two-index DOI/arXiv cross-checks, meaning verification ("A citation is valid only if the source actually supports the specific number, quote, or conclusion attached to it"), removal of unsourced claims, and no fake certainty. The question is whether the runtime behavior matches the prompt, and whether the eval can see the difference.

### 7.1 Fixture and ground truth

The fixture (`outputs/.probes/verifier-probe-draft.md`) contains six paragraphs:

| # | Claim | Ground truth |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lewis et al. 2020, RAG, arXiv:2005.11401, dense retriever + seq2seq, SOTA on three QA tasks | true |
| 2 | The same paper says RAG **underperforms** closed-book on all three tasks and scores **94.2%** EM on NQ | false; abstract says SOTA, and Table 1 reports 44.5 (RAG-Seq) / 44.1 (RAG-Token) vs. 34.5 (T5-11B) |
| 3 | [related work], *Retrieval Calibration for Long-Context Scientific Synthesis*, arXiv:2409.99999, +31% citation precision | fabricated ID and paper |
| 4 | Vaswani et al. 2017, *Attention Is All You Need*, arXiv:1706.03762, Transformer without recurrence/convolution | true |
| 5 | Komor et al. 2016, base editing without double-strand breaks | true, but no identifier |
| 6 | Feynman eval documented at `feynman.is/docs/evals/research-quality`, 12 questions, validity 71%→100% from 0.5.0 to 0.5.3 | URL is 404; 12 questions is true from the repo but not verifiable from the web; 71%→100% is false (committed validity was 100% in both) |

### 7.2 Clean run result

The clean run used a fresh `/tmp` workspace containing only `draft.md`; the transcript contains zero references to the probe fixtures or to `/work/...` paths (the only `/work` substrings are inside `crossref.org/works` and `openalex.org/works` URLs). It ran on `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, the same model as the lead in this session. Session-reported usage: 594,620 tokens, $0.0174, 31 tool calls, 82 seconds.

Manual rubric (n=1, not blinded):

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Fabricated paper removed or flagged | PASS | Removed; "arXiv has no record of 2409.99999, and a Semantic Scholar title search returned zero results" |
| False directional claim corrected | PASS | Replaced with 44.5/44.1 vs. 34.5 and "outperforming parametric seq2seq models" |
| False 94.2% removed | PASS | "the value 94.2 does not appear in the paper" |
| Dead URL flagged | PASS | Removed paragraph; "returns HTTP 404; no archived copy or indexed eval page was found" |
| True claims retained | PASS | Lewis, Vaswani, Komor all retained |
| Uncited true claim given a source | PASS | Komor DOI + PMID added |
| Unsupported 71%→100% removed | PASS | Removed with the paragraph |
| Inline citations + Sources, no orphans | PASS | 3 sources, [1]–[3] all cited |
| No new fabricated sources | PASS | arXiv + DOI + PubMed records resolve |
| Input draft unmodified | PASS | SHA-256 identical before/after |

The verifier also demonstrated a precision/recall tradeoff: it removed the true "12 questions" fact because it could not verify it from the web, even though the repository contains `evals/questions.jsonl` with 12 entries. Under its instructions ("if a factual claim cannot be traced to any source in the research files, either find a source for it or remove it"), removal was correct. But a research report that deletes true-but-unverifiable context is less comprehensive, and the eval's `key_recall` would not notice because "12 questions" is not a key paper.

### 7.3 The contaminated run is the more instructive one

The first verifier run used `/work` as its workspace, where my probe fixtures (`experiments/eval-scorer-probe.mjs`, `eval-scorer-probe-results.json`) were present. The verifier found them, used P3 to identify the fake paper, and wrote in its output: "The same title/ID pair appears in the local probe fixture as a deliberately fabricated citation (`experiments/eval-scorer-probe.mjs`, probe P3)." Nine transcript references to `eval-scorer-probe` confirm the leak.

That run is **not** a capability measurement; it is a demonstration of fixture leakage. It also shows why the harness's own per-question isolation matters: an eval that leaves its answer key or probe fixtures in the agent's workspace measures the agent's ability to find the answer key. The clean rerun is the one reported above.

A second contamination channel is model-level: the 12 questions and their expected key papers are public in the repository, and most key papers are famous. A model that memorized "Snell 2024 = 2408.03314" can satisfy `key_recall` without retrieval. The eval has no private holdout, no canary, and no post-cutoff question set. This is the classic benchmark-overfitting risk identified by Kapoor et al. [1].

---

## 8. Reliability, contamination, and reporting

### 8.1 Reliability

| Property | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Repeated runs per configuration | none | one row per question per config |
| Confidence intervals | none in results | I computed Wilson CI for 4/4: [0.51, 1.00] |
| Paired comparisons | partial | same four questions, but different subsets for Opus |
| Statistical test | none | 4/4 vs. 3/4 Fisher *p* = 1.0; 4/4 vs. 2/4 *p* = 0.43 |
| Model variance | none | one model per run; all agents inherit it |
| Prompt/runtime ablation | confounded | prompt changes ship with Pi/runtime updates in the same releases |
| Timeout sensitivity | high | one 45-minute timeout; 18M tokens |
| Cost variance | unmeasured | `$0.00` in every table |

The eval is a **single-shot smoke test**. That is a legitimate design for a pre-release check, but it is not enough to support "0.5.3 is better than 0.5.2" or "100% citation validity" as stable properties.

### 8.2 Contamination

| Channel | Risk | Current control |
|---|---|---|
| Public questions + expected papers | high for famous papers | none; questions are committed |
| Public LitQA2 items | medium | none; three items are redistributed |
| Repo access during a run | low in the eval's isolated workspace, high in a normal repo checkout | eval uses a temp workspace; normal runs do not |
| Probe/fixture leakage | demonstrated | none in the harness; my first probe failed this |
| Model memorization | high for classics | none; no private holdout |
| Canary/held-out set | absent | none |

The eval's isolation protects against **cross-question** contamination, not **training-data** contamination. The README's "keep the set fixed" rule preserves comparability but also preserves saturation.

### 8.3 Reporting

| Issue | Observation |
|---|---|
| Headline hides denominators | table shows `valid` but not `citations_checked`; in committed rows they are equal, so no observed inflation, but the code excludes failed lookups |
| Headline hides failure detail | `unresolved` and `title_mismatch` are in JSONL but not in the Markdown table |
| Cost is zero | no `cost` block in `models.json`; token counts are the only resource signal |
| Version labels disagree | filenames and Markdown summaries say 0.5.3/0.5.2; JSONL says 0.5.3/0.5.2/0.5.0; one SHA is absent |
| Dirty trees | 4 of 6 result files record `git_dirty: true` |
| Workdirs are local | macOS `/Users/...` and `/var/folders/...` paths; `--rescore` is not portable |
| Eval not shipped | `package.json` `files` omits `evals/`; users cannot run the vendor's eval from the installed package |
| No CI gate | no `evals/` reference in `.github/workflows/` or `package.json` scripts |

### 8.4 Cadence

The last committed eval result is 2026-09-24. The repository now contains 66 release sections after 0.5.3 (0.5.4 through 0.5.69) and 10 commits touching the prompts, agents, system prompt, or skills after the last eval commit. There is no automated gate. The README's own rule — "Run the eval before and after any change to prompts ... tools, extensions, or the Pi version" — is a manual convention. No eval result was committed after 2026-09-24, so for the last two months of releases the eval was either not run or not recorded.

This is the single highest-leverage process fix. An eval that is not run on the change it is meant to guard is documentation, not measurement.

## 9. Scorecard

Author judgment, grounded in the evidence above. "Strong" means the property is designed and demonstrated; "adequate" means present but thin; "weak" means present but not discriminating; "absent" means not implemented.

| Criterion | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Construct validity | **weak** | Measures bibliographic integrity, not claim faithfulness or research quality |
| Criterion validity (vs. experts) | **absent** | No human ratings, no agreement study, no correlation with expert judgment |
| Reliability / variance | **weak** | One run per config, four questions, no CIs |
| Reproducibility | **mixed** | Deterministic scorer, SHA/version/dirty captured, isolated runs; but dirty trees, a dangling SHA, local-only workdirs, not shipped, no CI |
| Contamination resistance | **weak** | Public fixed set, famous key papers, no private holdout or canary |
| Cost accounting | **absent** | `$0.00` everywhere; tokens only |
| Reporting / uncertainty | **mixed** | Raw JSONL and failures retained; table hides denominators, cost, and version mismatches |
| Coverage | **weak** | 4 of 12 questions exercised; 8 never run in the committed record |
| Runtime verification | **promising, unmeasured** | Verifier prompt is strong; clean probe passed 10/10; same-model judge, n=1; eval does not measure it |
| Process integration | **weak** | No CI gate; eval stale since 2026-09-24 while 66 releases landed |

**Overall:** a good **citation-integrity smoke test** with strong isolation and trace capture, wearing the label of a research-quality eval. The gap is not incompetence; the README names the missing lanes. The gap is between what the instrument measures and what its headline numbers are used to imply.

36:**What the committed evidence shows.** In all 22 committed rows, citation validity is 100% in every row that has citations, and key-paper recall is 100% in every completed row. The only pass/fail variation is completion: 4/4, 3/4, 2/4, 2/2, and one 45-minute timeout. The eval has never registered an unresolved citation in a completed run. Title match is 97–100%, with five mismatches across two rows. In other words, on the public record the eval is primarily a **completion detector** with a bibliographic sanity check, not a research-quality gradient.
38:**Provenance is weaker than the table suggests.** The headline 0.5.3 runs were made on a **dirty tree** (`git_dirty: true`) at commit `c1e0b29`, whose `package.json` says `0.5.2`; the recorded version field says `0.5.3`. The commit that adds the `bg_wait` rule the summary says was included is a *descendant* of that eval commit. One committed result row references a git SHA (`d926547`) that does not exist in the public repository. The workdirs are local macOS paths under `/Users/advaitpaliwal/...` or `/var/folders/...`, so `--rescore` cannot be reproduced from the repository alone.
42:**Cost is unmeasured.** Every committed table reports `$0.00` because the provider entry in `models.json` has no `cost` block. Token counts are large and heavy-tailed: 3.34M tokens per question for the 0.5.3 Terra run, 5.48M for the 0.5.3 Opus run, and 18.05M for the baseline's timed-out q10. A failed question consumed 28% of its run's tokens.
104:3. **Trace capture.** The result row records `git_sha`, `git_dirty`, `feynman_version`, model, `workdir`, per-question token usage, and the full session JSONL. That is enough to audit a run after the fact, even if the workdir is later deleted.
224:**The before/after comparison is underpowered.** The final 0.5.3 Terra run completed 4/4; the pre-wait 0.5.2 run completed 3/4. Fisher exact two-sided *p* = 1.0. The final 0.5.3 Opus run completed 2/2; the pre-wait 0.5.2 Opus run completed 2/4; *p* = 0.43. With four questions and one run per arm, the eval cannot distinguish the prompt change from noise. The Wilson 95% CI for 4/4 is [0.51, 1.00].

Nine transcript references to `eval-scorer-probe` confirm the leak.

# Verification review: `feynman-harness-eval-quality-case-study.md`

**Target:** `/work/outputs/feynman-harness-eval-quality-case-study.md` (44,929 bytes; SHA-256 `0bbea6b0c96db14a8488f450bcbb6c3217da06269180d73fe1f8f7c3752fb726`).
**Review mode:** evidence audit, not peer review. The report was re-read at 08:51 UTC after an 08:44:51 update; this review covers the current text. Two earlier issues — "seven committed result files" and "each configuration was run once on four questions" — are already fixed to "six" and "most on four, one on two" and are not flagged below.

---

## Summary

The report's central thesis is well supported by the artifacts. The committed eval is a deterministic bibliographic/completion smoke test, not a claim-faithfulness eval: the scorer is blind to negation and to URL/author-year citations (P4/P5/P8), zero-citation rows disappear from the aggregate, `done` is file existence, transparent removal is penalized (75% vs. 100%), and the clean runtime verifier caught errors the scorer cannot see. I reproduced nearly every table row and every token/wall/citation total exactly against `evals/results/*.jsonl`, the probe outputs, and the verifier transcripts.

Four evidence-integrity problems remain. One is a wrong Fisher *p*-value attached to the Opus comparison; one is an overstated trace-capture claim ("audit … even if the workdir is later deleted"); one is an undisclosed manual re-score of q01 citation validity that qualifies the "zero variance" headline; the rest are smaller precision, attribution, and inventory errors. No fabricated result or thesis-invalidating error was found.

---

## Strengths (what checked out)

- **Table 5.1 reproduces exactly.** Cites 51/43/28/54/44/85; validity 100% in every row with citations; title 97/100/100/100/97; recall 75/100/75/50/100/100; wall 7,895/2,806/2,724/2,459/2,508/2,199; tokens 72,190,181/14,053,916/14,073,816/13,039,960/13,353,797/10,953,040; cost `$0` per row / `$0.00` aggregate.
- **Row-level counts.** 22 rows; 4 of 6 result files dirty; five title mismatches (2 in baseline q01, 3 in final Opus q10); baseline q10 timed out at 2,700 s with 18,029,830 tokens; pre-wait Terra q04 consumed 3,968,890 tokens (28.2%).
- **Provenance checks.** `d926547` is not a valid object; `c1e0b29`'s `package.json` says `0.5.2`; `b1c4231` is a descendant of `c1e0b29` and adds the `bg_wait` line; `8e7efc5` is the last change to `evals/run.mjs`; `evals/run.mjs` SHA-256 is `23ba3bff…`; HEAD is `1174429`; package version is `0.5.69`; the installed CLI reports `0.5.65`.
- **Cadence checks.** RELEASES.md has 66 sections from 0.5.4 through 0.5.69; 10 commits touch `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`, or `skills/` after the last eval commit (also 10 from `e2bcb84`); no `evals/` reference in `.github/workflows/` or package scripts; `git diff v0.5.65..HEAD -- prompts/ .feynman/agents/` is empty.
- **Probe checks.** 8/8 probes match expectations; P4/P5/P8 gaps; table probe and `done` probe match the report; verifier scoring is 66.7% / 75.0% / 100.0%.
- **Clean verifier checks.** 594,620 tokens = 36,576 input + 10,460 output + 547,584 cache read; $0.0174; 31 `toolResult` records; 82.8 s from start to completion; zero `eval-scorer-probe` references in the clean transcript; draft SHA-256 unchanged.
- **Question set.** 12 questions; 6 Feynman-search-bench, 3 verbatim LitQA2, 3 hand-authored; only q01/q04/q07/q10 committed; 8 never run.
- **External citations.** arXiv 2407.01502, 2407.10362, 2506.11763, and 2508.15804 match the titles and authors in the report.

---

## Weaknesses (prioritized)

### MAJOR

**M1. Fisher *p* = 0.43 is attached to the wrong comparison.**
> "The final 0.5.3 Opus run completed 2/2; the pre-wait 0.5.2 Opus run completed 2/4; *p* = 0.43." (Section 5.2)

`experiments/eval-stats.log` records: "completion 4/4 (final) vs 2/4 (pre-wait Opus), Fisher exact two-sided p = 0.4286". That is final **Terra** (4/4) vs pre-wait **Opus** (2/4), a cross-model comparison — not final Opus (2/2) vs pre-wait Opus (2/4). Fisher for 2/2 vs 2/4 is **0.4667** (exact two-sided). Section 8.1 repeats "4/4 vs. 2/4 *p* = 0.43" without labeling the models, so one p-value is used for two different pairs. The qualitative conclusion ("underpowered") survives, but the number and pairing do not.

**M2. The "trace capture" claim is false about workdir deletion.**
> "The result row records `git_sha`, `git_dirty`, `feynman_version`, model, `workdir`, per-question token usage, and the full session JSONL. That is enough to audit a run after the fact, even if the workdir is later deleted." (Section 3, Strength #3)

The JSONL row records `workdir` and `usage.session_files` (a count), not the session JSONL content. The session JSONL lives inside the workdir (`evals/README.md`: the workdir holds "the full workspace, session JSONL and `feynman.log`"). If the workdir is deleted, the session is gone; the baseline workdirs are `/var/folders/...` temp paths. The report's own Section 8.3 ("workdirs are local; `--rescore` is not portable") and Recommendation #10 ("Commit … session JSONLs") contradict the claim.

**M3. The "zero variance / never failed" headline omits a documented manual re-score.**
> "**Citation validity has never failed on a completed run.** Across all 22 rows, every completed row with citations reports `citation_validity = 1.0`. The metric has zero observed variance in the public record." (Section 5.2)

Both pre-wait result summaries state: "q01 citation validity was re-scored after a transient lookup failure." (`evals/results/2026-09-24-lit-0.5.3-pre-wait-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.md` and the Opus counterpart.) The committed 100% is post-rescore; the raw first-pass denominator/score is not in the record. This qualifies "zero observed variance" and "never registered a failure," and it is the one place where the "failures are retained" strength is weaker than stated. The report's Section 8.3 correctly notes that the code excludes failed lookups, but it does not connect that to the re-score note.

### MINOR

**m1. 18.05M is the per-question mean, not q10.**
> "18.05M for the baseline's timed-out q10." (Section 1)

q10 is 18,029,830 (18.03M); 18,047,545 (18.05M) is the four-question mean. Section 5.2 gets this right ("18,029,830 … 25.0%").

**m2. "One committed result row references d926547" — it is four rows.**
> "One committed result row references a git SHA (`d926547`) that does not exist in the public repository." (Section 1; also Section 5.1 footnote)

`2026-09-24-lit-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.jsonl` has four rows, all with `d926547`. Say "one result file (four rows)."

**m3. "Nine transcript references" is not reproducible.**
> "Nine transcript references to `eval-scorer-probe` confirm the leak." (Section 7.3)

The contaminated transcript (`/state/.feynman/sessions/subagent-artifacts/a1f6227c-9de8-4bf5-961e-6d6806898d71_verifier_transcript.jsonl`) has 65 substring occurrences of `eval-scorer-probe` across 15 JSONL records; 5 `toolResult` records mention it; 4 tool calls use the probe paths. "Nine" matches none of these counts. The leak itself is unambiguous.

**m4. The `/work` parenthetical is incomplete.**
> "the only `/work` substrings are inside `crossref.org/works` and `openalex.org/works` URLs." (Section 7.2)

The clean transcript also contains `feynman.is/docs/workflows/review/`, `/deep-research/`, and `/literature-review/` URLs. The substantive claim — zero references to the probe fixtures — holds (0 `eval-scorer-probe` hits).

**m5. "last two months of releases" is ~7 weeks.**
> "for the last two months of releases the eval was either not run or not recorded." (Section 8.4)

0.5.3 (2026-09-24) to 0.5.69 (2026-11-13) is 50 days. Say "the last ~7 weeks" or "since 0.5.3."

**m6. The zero-cost cause is inferred, not verified.**
> "Every committed table reports `$0.00` because the provider entry in `models.json` has no `cost` block." (Section 1)

`models.json` is not in the repository; the committed runs used an external file. The README says cost is 0 when no cost block exists, and all `usage.cost_usd` are 0, so the inference is plausible, but "because" is not directly checkable from the repository. Phrase as "consistent with the documented behavior" or "the committed rows record no cost."

**m7. "Title match is 97–100%" is aggregate.**
> "Title match is 97–100%, with five mismatches across two rows." (Section 1)

The 97% values are means; the underlying rows are 92.3% (baseline q01) and 93.0% (final Opus q10). The "five mismatches" sentence mitigates, but "row-level title match ranges 92–100%; aggregate means 97–100%" would be precise.

**m8. The v0.5.3 release note's 0.5.2 comparison is also inconsistent, and the report does not flag it.**
`RELEASES.md` line 476: "(0.5.2: 9-14 minutes, 43 of 43 citations)". The committed 0.5.2 pre-wait rows have 28 citations and 3/4 completion; 43/43 is the 0.5.0 Terra file. The report flags the Markdown summary's "0.5.2 run" pointing at a 0.5.0 file, but not this release-note instance of the same mislabel.

**m9. The Opus 2/2 subset is explained by refusals, which the report does not mention.**
The 0.5.3 Opus summary says: "Only the non-biology questions were run: Opus 5.5 refuses q04 and q07." The report's "different subsets for Opus" and "4 of 12 questions exercised" are true, but the refusal cause is relevant to coverage and model variance.

**m10. Appendix B omits the transcripts and `experiments/score-verifier-output.log`.**
The contamination claims rely on transcripts; the inventory lists only the output files. The transcripts exist under `/state/.feynman/sessions/subagent-artifacts/` and the clean one has 0 fixture references, so the claim is true, but the artifact inventory is incomplete.

**m11. Sources [2], [5], [7], [8] are not cited by number in the body.**
They are used in the question table and the verifier fixture, but only [1], [3], [4], [6] appear as bracketed citations. Either map them inline or label them as background.

**m12. "one runtime verification probe" vs. the provenance's "2 runtime verification probes."**
The report explains the contaminated attempt, so this is a wording inconsistency, not a substantive error.

---

## Questions for Authors

1. What was the pre-rescore q01 validity in the two pre-wait runs? Is the raw first-pass score recoverable from the workdir or logs?
2. For the 2/2 vs. 2/4 Opus comparison, what is the exact Fisher table and p-value you intend? (2/2 vs. 2/4 = 0.4667; 4/4 vs. 2/4 = 0.4286.)
3. Does the `terra-r2` / `opus-r2` workdir naming indicate an earlier uncommitted round? If so, does "one run per configuration" describe the committed record only?
4. Is the v0.5.3 release note's "0.5.2: 43 of 43" a third instance of the 0.5.0/0.5.2 mislabel?
5. Where is the clean verifier transcript archived, and should it be added to Appendix B?

---

## Verdict

**Verification verdict: pass with major corrections.** The central thesis and nearly all quantitative table rows are supported. The report should not circulate in its current form without fixing M1–M3; these are evidence-integrity issues, not stylistic ones. Confidence: high on the table/sum arithmetic and probe outputs; high on the p-value and trace-capture errors; medium on the magnitude of the re-score effect because the pre-rescore value is not recoverable.

---

## Revision Plan

1. **Fix M1.** Replace p = 0.43 for 2/2 vs. 2/4 with 0.47, or relabel it as the 4/4-vs-2/4 cross-model comparison; make Section 8.1 consistent.
2. **Fix M2.** Rewrite Strength #3 to say the row records the workdir path, not the session content; delete "even if the workdir is later deleted."
3. **Fix M3.** Add the q01 re-score note to Section 5.2 and the "zero variance" sentence; distinguish "as committed" from "as first run."
4. **Fix m1–m7.** 18.03M; four rows for `d926547`; transcript counts; `/work` parenthetical; "~7 weeks"; cost phrasing; row-level title range.
5. **Fix m8–m12.** Disclose the release-note 43/43, the Opus refusal cause, the missing Appendix B transcripts/log, the uncited sources, and the probe-count wording.

---

## Inline Annotations

> "The final 0.5.3 Opus run completed 2/2; the pre-wait 0.5.2 Opus run completed 2/4; *p* = 0.43."
**[M1] MAJOR:** The p-value in `eval-stats.log` (0.4286) belongs to 4/4 vs. 2/4, not 2/2 vs. 2/4. Correct p for the stated pair is 0.4667. Section 8.1 reuses the same p for "4/4 vs. 2/4," so the report is comparing two different pairs with one number.

## Summary

The report's central thesis is well supported by the artifacts. The committed eval is a deterministic bibliographic/completion smoke test, not a claim-faithfulness eval: the scorer is blind to negation and to URL/author-year citations (P4/P5/P8), zero-citation rows disappear from the aggregate, `done` is file existence, transparent removal is penalized (75% vs. 100%), and the clean runtime verifier caught errors the scorer cannot see. Four evidence-integrity problems remain. ## Weaknesses (prioritized)

### MAJOR

**M1. Fisher *p* = 0.43 is attached to the wrong comparison.**
> "The final 0.5.3 Opus run completed 2/2; the pre-wait 0.5.2 Opus run completed 2/4; *p* = 0.43." (Section 5.2)

`experiments/eval-stats.log` records: "completion 4/4 (final) vs 2/4 (pre-wait Opus), Fisher exact two-sided p = 0.4286". That is final **Terra** (4/4) vs pre-wait **Opus** (2/4), a cross-model comparison — not final Opus (2/2) vs pre-wait Opus (2/4). Fisher for 2/2 vs 2/4 is **0.4667** (exact two-sided). Section 8.1 repeats "4/4 vs. 2/4 *p* = 0.43" without labeling the models, so one p-value is used for two different pairs. The qualitative conclusion ("underpowered") survives, but the number and pairing do not.

**M2. The "trace capture" claim is false about workdir deletion.**
> "The result row records `git_sha`, `git_dirty`, `feynman_version`, model, `workdir`, per-question token usage, and the full session JSONL. That is enough to audit a run after the fact, even if the workdir is later deleted." (Section 3, Strength #3)

The JSONL row records `workdir` and `usage.session_files` (a count), not the session JSONL content. The session JSONL lives inside the workdir (`evals/README.md`: the workdir holds "the full workspace, session JSONL and `feynman.log`"). If the workdir is deleted, the session is gone; the baseline workdirs are `/var/folders/...` temp paths. The report's own Section 8.3 ("workdirs are local; `--rescore` is not portable") and Recommendation #10 ("Commit … session JSONLs") contradict the claim.

**M3. The "zero variance / never failed" headline omits a documented manual re-score.**
> "**Citation validity has never failed on a completed run.** Across all 22 rows, every completed row with citations reports `citation_validity = 1.0`. The metric has zero observed variance in the public record." (Section 5.2)

Both pre-wait result summaries state: "q01 citation validity was re-scored after a transient lookup failure." (`evals/results/2026-09-24-lit-0.5.3-pre-wait-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.md` and the Opus counterpart.) The committed 100% is post-rescore; the raw first-pass denominator/score is not in the record. This qualifies "zero observed variance" and "never registered a failure," and it is the one place where the "failures are retained" strength is weaker than stated. The report's Section 8.3 correctly notes that the code excludes failed lookups, but it does not connect that to the re-score note.

### MINOR

> "18.05M for the baseline's timed-out q10." (Section 1)

q10 is 18,029,830 (18.03M); 18,047,545 (18.05M) is the four-question mean. Section 5.2 gets this right ("18,029,830 … 25.0%").

**m2. "One committed result row references d926547" — it is four rows.**
> "One committed result row references a git SHA (`d926547`) that does not exist in the public repository." (Section 1; also Section 5.1 footnote)

`2026-09-24-lit-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.jsonl` has four rows, all with `d926547`. Say "one result file (four rows)."

**m3. "Nine transcript references" is not reproducible.**

"Nine" matches none of these counts. The leak itself is unambiguous.

> "the only `/work` substrings are inside `crossref.org/works` and `openalex.org/works` URLs." (Section 7.2)

The clean transcript also contains `feynman.is/docs/workflows/review/`, `/deep-research/`, and `/literature-review/` URLs. The substantive claim — zero references to the probe fixtures — holds (0 `eval-scorer-probe` hits).

**m5. "last two months of releases" is ~7 weeks.**
> "for the last two months of releases the eval was either not run or not recorded." (Section 8.4)

0.5.3 (2026-09-24) to 0.5.69 (2026-11-13) is 50 days. Say "the last ~7 weeks" or "since 0.5.3."

`models.json` is not in the repository; the committed runs used an external file. **Target:** `/work/outputs/feynman-harness-eval-quality-case-study.md` (44,929 bytes; SHA-256 `0bbea6b0c96db14a8488f450bcbb6c3217da06269180d73fe1f8f7c3752fb726`).

Two earlier issues — "seven committed result files" and "each configuration was run once on four questions" — are already fixed to "six" and "most on four, one on two" and are not flagged below.

---

## Summary

The report's central thesis is well supported by the artifacts. The committed eval is a deterministic bibliographic/completion smoke test, not a claim-faithfulness eval: the scorer is blind to negation and to URL/author-year citations (P4/P5/P8), zero-citation rows disappear from the aggregate, `done` is file existence, transparent removal is penalized (75% vs. 100%), and the clean runtime verifier caught errors the scorer cannot see. I reproduced nearly every table row and every token/wall/citation total exactly against `evals/results/*.jsonl`, the probe outputs, and the verifier transcripts.

Four evidence-integrity problems remain. One is a wrong Fisher *p*-value attached to the Opus comparison; one is an overstated trace-capture claim ("audit … even if the workdir is later deleted"); one is an undisclosed manual re-score of q01 citation validity that qualifies the "zero variance" headline; the rest are smaller precision, attribution, and inventory errors. No fabricated result or thesis-invalidating error was found.

---

## Strengths (what checked out)

- **Table 5.1 reproduces exactly.** Cites 51/43/28/54/44/85; validity 100% in every row with citations; title 97/100/100/100/97; recall 75/100/75/50/100/100; wall 7,895/2,806/2,724/2,459/2,508/2,199; tokens 72,190,181/14,053,916/14,073,816/13,039,960/13,353,797/10,953,040; cost `$0` per row / `$0.00` aggregate.
- **Row-level counts.** 22 rows; 4 of 6 result files dirty; five title mismatches (2 in baseline q01, 3 in final Opus q10); baseline q10 timed out at 2,700 s with 18,029,830 tokens; pre-wait Terra q04 consumed 3,968,890 tokens (28.2%).
- **Provenance checks.** `d926547` is not a valid object; `c1e0b29`'s `package.json` says `0.5.2`; `b1c4231` is a descendant of `c1e0b29` and adds the `bg_wait` line; `8e7efc5` is the last change to `evals/run.mjs`; `evals/run.mjs` SHA-256 is `23ba3bff…`; HEAD is `1174429`; package version is `0.5.69`; the installed CLI reports `0.5.65`.
- **Cadence checks.** RELEASES.md has 66 sections from 0.5.4 through 0.5.69; 10 commits touch `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`, or `skills/` after the last eval commit (also 10 from `e2bcb84`); no `evals/` reference in `.github/workflows/` or package scripts; `git diff v0.5.65..HEAD -- prompts/ .feynman/agents/` is empty.
- **Probe checks.** 8/8 probes match expectations; P4/P5/P8 gaps; table probe and `done` probe match the report; verifier scoring is 66.7% / 75.0% / 100.0%.
- **Clean verifier checks.** 594,620 tokens = 36,576 input + 10,460 output + 547,584 cache read; $0.0174; 31 `toolResult` records; 82.8 s from start to completion; zero `eval-scorer-probe` references in the clean transcript; draft SHA-256 unchanged.
- **Question set.** 12 questions; 6 Feynman-search-bench, 3 verbatim LitQA2, 3 hand-authored; only q01/q04/q07/q10 committed; 8 never run.
- **External citations.** arXiv 2407.01502, 2407.10362, 2506.11763, and 2508.15804 match the titles and authors in the report.

---

## Weaknesses (prioritized)

### MAJOR

**M1. Fisher *p* = 0.43 is attached to the wrong comparison.**
> "The final 0.5.3 Opus run completed 2/2; the pre-wait 0.5.2 Opus run completed 2/4; *p* = 0.43." (Section 5.2)

`experiments/eval-stats.log` records: "completion 4/4 (final) vs 2/4 (pre-wait Opus), Fisher exact two-sided p = 0.4286". That is final **Terra** (4/4) vs pre-wait **Opus** (2/4), a cross-model comparison — not final Opus (2/2) vs pre-wait Opus (2/4). Fisher for 2/2 vs 2/4 is **0.4667** (exact two-sided). Section 8.1 repeats "4/4 vs. 2/4 *p* = 0.43" without labeling the models, so one p-value is used for two different pairs. The qualitative conclusion ("underpowered") survives, but the number and pairing do not.

**M2. The "trace capture" claim is false about workdir deletion.**
> "The result row records `git_sha`, `git_dirty`, `feynman_version`, model, `workdir`, per-question token usage, and the full session JSONL. That is enough to audit a run after the fact, even if the workdir is later deleted." (Section 3, Strength #3)

The JSONL row records `workdir` and `usage.session_files` (a count), not the session JSONL content. The session JSONL lives inside the workdir (`evals/README.md`: the workdir holds "the full workspace, session JSONL and `feynman.log`"). If the workdir is deleted, the session is gone; the baseline workdirs are `/var/folders/...` temp paths. The report's own Section 8.3 ("workdirs are local; `--rescore` is not portable") and Recommendation #10 ("Commit … session JSONLs") contradict the claim.

**M3. The "zero variance / never failed" headline omits a documented manual re-score.**
> "**Citation validity has never failed on a completed run.** Across all 22 rows, every completed row with citations reports `citation_validity = 1.0`. The metric has zero observed variance in the public record." (Section 5.2)

Both pre-wait result summaries state: "q01 citation validity was re-scored after a transient lookup failure." (`evals/results/2026-09-24-lit-0.5.3-pre-wait-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.md` and the Opus counterpart.) The committed 100% is post-rescore; the raw first-pass denominator/score is not in the record. This qualifies "zero observed variance" and "never registered a failure," and it is the one place where the "failures are retained" strength is weaker than stated. The report's Section 8.3 correctly notes that the code excludes failed lookups, but it does not connect that to the re-score note.

### MINOR

**m1. 18.05M is the per-question mean, not q10.**
> "18.05M for the baseline's timed-out q10." (Section 1)

q10 is 18,029,830 (18.03M); 18,047,545 (18.05M) is the four-question mean. Section 5.2 gets this right ("18,029,830 … 25.0%").

**m2. "One committed result row references d926547" — it is four rows.**
> "One committed result row references a git SHA (`d926547`) that does not exist in the public repository." (Section 1; also Section 5.1 footnote)

`2026-09-24-lit-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.jsonl` has four rows, all with `d926547`. Say "one result file (four rows)."

**m3. "Nine transcript references" is not reproducible.**

# Feynman 0.5.65 as an evaluation instrument

**A dogfooded case study of an AI research harness, judged by AI-eval-quality criteria**

- **Date:** 2026-11-14
- **Harness under study:** Feynman `0.5.65` (installed), repository HEAD `0.5.69`
- **Study type:** static audit + deterministic meta-eval + one runtime verification probe
- **Canonical artifact:** `outputs/feynman-harness-eval-quality-case-study.md`
- **Raw artifacts:** `experiments/eval-scorer-probe.mjs`, `experiments/eval-scorer-probe-results.json`, `experiments/score-verifier-output.mjs`, `experiments/verifier-output-score.json`, `outputs/.probes/`

---

## 0. Scope and method

This is a case study of Feynman as an **evaluation instrument**, not a benchmark of its research prose. The question is: when Feynman reports that a research workflow scored 100%, what has actually been measured, how repeatable is it, and what would a careful eval engineer conclude?

I used four kinds of evidence:

1. **Static audit** of the installed package, the public repository, the workflow prompts, the four bundled subagents, and the `evals/` directory.
2. **Deterministic meta-eval** of Feynman's own citation scorer: eight synthetic outputs with known ground truth, plus probes of the `done` metric and the aggregate table. The scorer was imported from a generated copy of `evals/run.mjs` with only the CLI entrypoint removed; no scoring logic was reimplemented.
3. **Runtime verification probe**: a short draft with one fabricated paper, one false quantitative claim, one false directional claim, one dead URL, one uncited true claim, and two true citations, given to Feynman's `verifier` subagent in a clean workspace. The first attempt was contaminated by probe fixtures in the same workspace and is reported as a negative control, not as a capability measurement.
4. **Re-analysis of the six committed result files** (JSONL plus matching Markdown summaries) in `evals/results/`, including their recorded git SHA, dirty flag, version, token usage, and per-row failures.

**Explicit non-goals:** I did not run the full 12-question eval (it would cost millions of tokens per question and hours of wall time), did not recruit human raters, and did not inspect Feynman's private telemetry or internal eval history. The study is therefore a close reading of the public instrument plus small controlled probes, not a leaderboard run.

A reflexivity warning applies throughout: I am the harness being studied. I read `evals/questions.jsonl` before designing the probes. The deterministic probes are resistant to that observer effect because their expectations are fixed in code; the runtime verifier probe is not blinded and is reported as `n=1`.

---

## 1. Executive summary

**What is good.** Feynman ships a real research-quality eval, not a vibes-based demo. It uses deterministic checks against arXiv, Crossref, and doi.org, with no LLM judge. Each question runs in an isolated temp workspace and isolated `FEYNMAN_HOME`, with telemetry off. Every row records the git SHA, dirty flag, Feynman version, model, wall time, token usage, failures, and the workdir containing the full session. Failures are kept in the results rather than deleted. The README states its own limitations ("Treat a single run as noisy"; "read the listed rows before calling something a hallucination"). These are practices many agent evals do not have.

**What is measured.** The headline metrics are bibliographic: whether cited arXiv IDs and DOIs resolve, whether the resolved title appears near the identifier, whether expected key papers are present, and whether the final output plus a provenance sidecar exist. They do **not** measure whether the sentence attached to a citation is true. A sentence that says a paper found the *opposite* of its central claim still scores 100% on title match, because the title tokens are present and the negation is invisible to a bag-of-words overlap check.

**What the committed evidence shows.** In all 22 committed rows, citation validity is 100% in every row that has citations, and key-paper recall is 100% in every completed row. The only pass/fail variation is completion, on differing question subsets: 4/4, 3/4, 2/4, 2/2, and one 45-minute timeout. The eval has never registered an unresolved citation in a completed run. Title match is 97–100%, with five mismatches across two rows. In other words, on the public record the eval is primarily a **completion detector** with a bibliographic sanity check, not a research-quality gradient.

**Provenance is weaker than the table suggests.** The headline 0.5.3 runs were made on a **dirty tree** (`git_dirty: true`) at commit `c1e0b29`, whose `package.json` says `0.5.2`; the recorded version field says `0.5.3`. The commit that adds the `bg_wait` rule the summary says was included is a *descendant* of that eval commit. One committed result row references a git SHA (`d926547`) that does not exist in the public repository. The workdirs are local macOS paths under `/Users/advaitpaliwal/...` or `/var/folders/...`, so `--rescore` cannot be reproduced from the repository alone.

**Cadence and statistics are thin.** The last committed eval result is dated 2026-09-24 and scored 0.5.3-era prompts. Since then, 66 release sections (0.5.4–0.5.69) and 10 commits touching `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`, or `skills/` have landed. There is no reference to `evals/` in `.github/workflows/` or in any `package.json` script, so the eval is manual. Each configuration was run once; most on four questions, one on two. A 4/4 versus 3/4 completion difference is not statistically distinguishable (Fisher exact two-sided *p* = 1.0; Wilson 95% CI for 4/4 is [0.51, 1.00]).

**Cost is unmeasured.** Every committed table reports `$0.00` because the provider entry in `models.json` has no `cost` block. Token counts are large and heavy-tailed: 3.34M tokens per question for the 0.5.3 Terra run, 5.48M for the 0.5.3 Opus run, and 18.05M for the baseline's timed-out q10. A failed question consumed 28% of its run's tokens.

**The runtime verifier caught errors the eval cannot see.** In a clean workspace, the `verifier` subagent caught the fabricated arXiv ID, corrected the false RAG claim with the paper's actual 44.5 vs. 34.5 exact-match numbers, removed the fabricated 94.2%, flagged the dead URL, and added a missing DOI/PubMed source. It did this in 82 seconds for 594,620 tokens and $0.0174 (session-reported). But its corrections are largely invisible to the eval scorer. Worse, a transparent verifier that documents a removed fake ID in a "Removed Unsupported Claims" section is *penalized* by the scorer, while a verifier that silently deletes the fake scores higher: 75% vs. 100% citation validity in the controlled probe.

**Bottom line.** Feynman's eval is a credible **citation-integrity smoke test** with unusually good isolation and trace capture. It is not yet a research-quality eval: it lacks claim-level faithfulness, human calibration, repeated runs, a private holdout, cost accounting, and a release gate. Its own roadmap says as much: the README lists ScholarQA-CS2, DeepResearch Bench FACT, and SciCoQA as "next lanes, not built yet."

---

## 2. The object: what the eval actually is

A reflexivity warning applies throughout: I am the harness being studied. I read `evals/questions.jsonl` before designing the probes. The deterministic probes are resistant to that observer effect because their expectations are fixed in code; the runtime verifier probe is not blinded and is reported as `n=1`.

---

## 1. Executive summary

**What is good.** Feynman ships a real research-quality eval, not a vibes-based demo. It uses deterministic checks against arXiv, Crossref, and doi.org, with no LLM judge. Each question runs in an isolated temp workspace and isolated `FEYNMAN_HOME`, with telemetry off. Every row records the git SHA, dirty flag, Feynman version, model, wall time, token usage, failures, and the workdir containing the full session. Failures are kept in the results rather than deleted. The README states its own limitations ("Treat a single run as noisy"; "read the listed rows before calling something a hallucination"). These are practices many agent evals do not have.

**What is measured.** The headline metrics are bibliographic: whether cited arXiv IDs and DOIs resolve, whether the resolved title appears near the identifier, whether expected key papers are present, and whether the final output plus a provenance sidecar exist. They do **not** measure whether the sentence attached to a citation is true. A sentence that says a paper found the *opposite* of its central claim still scores 100% on title match, because the title tokens are present and the negation is invisible to a bag-of-words overlap check.

**What the committed evidence shows.** In all 22 committed rows, citation validity is 100% in every row that has citations, and key-paper recall is 100% in every completed row. The only pass/fail variation is completion, on differing question subsets: 4/4, 3/4, 2/4, 2/2, and one 45-minute timeout. The eval has never registered an unresolved citation in a completed run. Title match is 97–100%, with five mismatches across two rows. In other words, on the public record the eval is primarily a **completion detector** with a bibliographic sanity check, not a research-quality gradient.

**Provenance is weaker than the table suggests.** The headline 0.5.3 runs were made on a **dirty tree** (`git_dirty: true`) at commit `c1e0b29`, whose `package.json` says `0.5.2`; the recorded version field says `0.5.3`. The commit that adds the `bg_wait` rule the summary says was included is a *descendant* of that eval commit. One committed result row references a git SHA (`d926547`) that does not exist in the public repository. The workdirs are local macOS paths under `/Users/advaitpaliwal/...` or `/var/folders/...`, so `--rescore` cannot be reproduced from the repository alone.

**Cadence and statistics are thin.** The last committed eval result is dated 2026-09-24 and scored 0.5.3-era prompts. Since then, 66 release sections (0.5.4–0.5.69) and 10 commits touching `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`, or `skills/` have landed. There is no reference to `evals/` in `.github/workflows/` or in any `package.json` script, so the eval is manual. Each configuration was run once; most on four questions, one on two. A 4/4 versus 3/4 completion difference is not statistically distinguishable (Fisher exact two-sided *p* = 1.0; Wilson 95% CI for 4/4 is [0.51, 1.00]).

**Cost is unmeasured.** Every committed table reports `$0.00` because the provider entry in `models.json` has no `cost` block. Token counts are large and heavy-tailed: 3.34M tokens per question for the 0.5.3 Terra run, 5.48M for the 0.5.3 Opus run, and 18.05M for the baseline's timed-out q10. A failed question consumed 28% of its run's tokens.

**The runtime verifier caught errors the eval cannot see.** In a clean workspace, the `verifier` subagent caught the fabricated arXiv ID, corrected the false RAG claim with the paper's actual 44.5 vs. 34.5 exact-match numbers, removed the fabricated 94.2%, flagged the dead URL, and added a missing DOI/PubMed source. It did this in 82 seconds for 594,620 tokens and $0.0174 (session-reported). But its corrections are largely invisible to the eval scorer. Worse, a transparent verifier that documents a removed fake ID in a "Removed Unsupported Claims" section is *penalized* by the scorer, while a verifier that silently deletes the fake scores higher: 75% vs. 100% citation validity in the controlled probe.

**Bottom line.** Feynman's eval is a credible **citation-integrity smoke test** with unusually good isolation and trace capture. It is not yet a research-quality eval: it lacks claim-level faithfulness, human calibration, repeated runs, a private holdout, cost accounting, and a release gate. Its own roadmap says as much: the README lists ScholarQA-CS2, DeepResearch Bench FACT, and SciCoQA as "next lanes, not built yet."

### 5.2 What the table reveals

**Citation validity has never failed on a completed run — as committed.** Across all 22 rows, every completed row with citations reports `citation_validity = 1.0`. The metric has zero observed variance in the committed record. That may mean the outputs are genuinely well-cited; it also means the metric has not demonstrated the ability to detect a bad citation outside the synthetic probe. One caveat: both pre-wait summaries state that q01 citation validity was re-scored after a transient lookup failure. The committed 100% is therefore post-rescore; the first-pass value is not in the record. "Never failed" describes the committed rows, not the raw first pass.

**Key-paper recall is a completion indicator, not a quality gradient.** In every completed row, `key_recall = 1.0`; in every incomplete row, `key_recall = 0.0`. It does not distinguish a strong report from a weak one on this set.

**Title match is the only quality score with observed variance:** five mismatches across two rows (two in the baseline q01, three in the 0.5.3 Opus q10). The README itself warns that short-name citations miss this check, so even these five are not necessarily errors.

**The before/after comparison is underpowered, and the Opus comparison is invalid.** The final 0.5.3 Terra run completed 4/4; the pre-wait 0.5.2 run completed 3/4. Fisher exact two-sided *p* = 1.0. The final 0.5.3 Opus run covers only q01 and q10; its summary says Opus 5.5 refuses the two biology questions (q04, q07), and the pre-wait run records both as exit-code-1 failures. So 2/2 versus 2/4 reflects a different question set, not a prompt effect. The only like-for-like before/after comparison is Terra: 4/4 versus 3/4, *p* = 1.0. With four questions and one run per arm, the eval cannot distinguish the prompt change from noise. The Wilson 95% CI for 4/4 is [0.51, 1.00].

# Verification review: `feynman-harness-eval-quality-case-study.md`

**Target:** `/work/outputs/feynman-harness-eval-quality-case-study.md` (45,696 bytes; SHA-256 `cbfe4d4232df88b80f7c91ef2f889389ac0e64923a9e7de5feb0f83e6a2a819a`).
**Review mode:** evidence audit, not peer review. The report was updated at 08:44:51 and again at 08:54:08; this review targets the 08:54:08 text. The 08:54:08 edit resolved two earlier findings (the q01 re-score omission and the Opus p-value misattribution in Section 5.2) and added "on differing question subsets" plus a `[10]` citation; the remaining issues are below.

---

## Summary

The report's central thesis is well supported by the artifacts. The committed eval is a deterministic bibliographic/completion smoke test, not a claim-faithfulness eval: the scorer is blind to negation and to URL/author-year citations (P4/P5/P8), zero-citation rows disappear from the aggregate, `done` is file existence, transparent removal is penalized (75% vs. 100%), and the clean runtime verifier caught errors the scorer cannot see. I reproduced nearly every table row and every token/wall/citation total exactly against `evals/results/*.jsonl`, the probe outputs, and the verifier transcripts.

Two major issues remain, plus a set of smaller precision, attribution, and inventory errors. Section 8.1's statistical table is now stale: it still prints "4/4 vs. 2/4 *p* = 0.43" and calls the Opus comparison "partial," while the corrected Section 5.2 says the Opus comparison is invalid and that the only like-for-like comparison is Terra. Separately, Strength #3's trace-capture claim is still false about workdir deletion. No fabricated result or thesis-invalidating error was found.

---

## Strengths (what checked out)

- **Table 5.1 reproduces exactly.** Cites 51/43/28/54/44/85; validity 100% in every row with citations; title 97/100/100/100/97; recall 75/100/75/50/100/100; wall 7,895/2,806/2,724/2,459/2,508/2,199; tokens 72,190,181/14,053,916/14,073,816/13,039,960/13,353,797/10,953,040; cost `$0` per row / `$0.00` aggregate.
- **Row-level counts.** 22 rows; 4 of 6 result files dirty; five title mismatches (2 in baseline q01, 3 in final Opus q10); baseline q10 timed out at 2,700 s with 18,029,830 tokens; pre-wait Terra q04 consumed 3,968,890 tokens (28.2%).
- **Provenance checks.** `d926547` is not a valid object; `c1e0b29`'s `package.json` says `0.5.2`; `b1c4231` is a descendant of `c1e0b29` and adds the `bg_wait` line; `8e7efc5` is the last change to `evals/run.mjs`; `evals/run.mjs` SHA-256 is `23ba3bff…`; HEAD is `1174429`; package version is `0.5.69`; the installed CLI reports `0.5.65`.
- **Cadence checks.** RELEASES.md has 66 sections from 0.5.4 through 0.5.69; 10 commits touch `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`, or `skills/` after the last eval commit (also 10 from `e2bcb84`); no `evals/` reference in `.github/workflows/` or package scripts; `git diff v0.5.65..HEAD -- prompts/ .feynman/agents/` is empty.
- **Probe checks.** 8/8 probes match expectations; P4/P5/P8 gaps; table probe and `done` probe match the report; verifier scoring is 66.7% / 75.0% / 100.0%.
- **Clean verifier checks.** 594,620 tokens = 36,576 input + 10,460 output + 547,584 cache read; $0.0174; 31 `toolResult` records; 82.8 s from start to completion; zero `eval-scorer-probe` references in the clean transcript; draft SHA-256 unchanged.
- **Question set.** 12 questions; 6 Feynman-search-bench, 3 verbatim LitQA2, 3 hand-authored; only q01/q04/q07/q10 committed; 8 never run.
- **External citations.** arXiv 2407.01502, 2407.10362, 2506.11763, and 2508.15804 match the titles and authors in the report.

---

## Weaknesses (prioritized)

### MAJOR

**M1. Section 8.1's statistical table is stale after the Section 5.2 correction.**
> "| Statistical test | none | 4/4 vs. 3/4 Fisher *p* = 1.0; 4/4 vs. 2/4 *p* = 0.43 |"
> "| Paired comparisons | partial | same four questions, but different subsets for Opus |" (Section 8.1)

Section 5.2 now correctly says: "So 2/2 versus 2/4 reflects a different question set, not a prompt effect. The only like-for-like before/after comparison is Terra: 4/4 versus 3/4, *p* = 1.0." But Section 8.1 still presents 4/4 vs. 2/4 *p* = 0.43 as a statistical test and calls the Opus comparison "partial." The p-value 0.4286 is arithmetically correct for 4/4 vs. 2/4 (final Terra vs. pre-wait Opus), but that is the cross-model comparison Section 5.2 rejects. The table should drop it or label it cross-model and non-paired; the "Paired comparisons" row should say the Opus pair is not comparable (different question sets) and only Terra is like-for-like.

**M2. The "trace capture" claim is false about workdir deletion.**
> "The result row records `git_sha`, `git_dirty`, `feynman_version`, model, `workdir`, per-question token usage, and the full session JSONL. That is enough to audit a run after the fact, even if the workdir is later deleted." (Section 3, Strength #3)

The JSONL row records `workdir` and `usage.session_files` (a count), not the session JSONL content. The session JSONL lives inside the workdir (`evals/README.md`: the workdir holds "the full workspace, session JSONL and `feynman.log`"). If the workdir is deleted, the session is gone; the baseline workdirs are `/var/folders/...` temp paths. The report's own Section 8.3 ("workdirs are local; `--rescore` is not portable") and Recommendation #10 ("Commit … session JSONLs") contradict the claim.

### Resolved during this pass

- **R1. q01 re-score disclosure.** The 08:54:08 text now says: "**Citation validity has never failed on a completed run — as committed.** … One caveat: both pre-wait summaries state that q01 citation validity was re-scored after a transient lookup failure. The committed 100% is therefore post-rescore; the first-pass value is not in the record. 'Never failed' describes the committed rows, not the raw first pass." This resolves the earlier omission; keep this wording.
- **R2. Opus comparison.** Section 5.2 now correctly says the Opus 2/2 vs. 2/4 comparison "reflects a different question set, not a prompt effect" and that the only like-for-like comparison is Terra. The old p = 0.43 sentence is gone. The remaining problem is only that Section 8.1 was not updated (M1).
- **R3. Result-file and configuration counts.** The current text says "six committed result files" and "Six `.md`/`.jsonl` pairs (six configurations)," and "Each configuration was run once; most on four questions, one on two." These are correct.

### MINOR

**m1. 18.05M is the per-question mean, not q10.**
> "18.05M for the baseline's timed-out q10." (Section 1)

q10 is 18,029,830 (18.03M); 18,047,545 (18.05M) is the four-question mean. Section 5.2 gets this right ("18,029,830 … 25.0%").

**m2. "One committed result row references d926547" — it is four rows.**
> "One committed result row references a git SHA (`d926547`) that does not exist in the public repository." (Section 1; also Section 5.1 footnote)

`2026-09-24-lit-ferrylane-openai_gpt-5.6-terra.jsonl` has four rows, all with `d926547`. Say "one result file (four rows)."

**m3. "Nine transcript references" is not reproducible.**
> "Nine transcript references to `eval-scorer-probe` confirm the leak." (Section 7.3)

The contaminated transcript (`/state/.feynman/sessions/subagent-artifacts/a1f6227c-9de8-4bf5-961e-6d6806898d71_verifier_transcript.jsonl`) has 65 substring occurrences of `eval-scorer-probe` across 15 JSONL records; 5 `toolResult` records mention it; 4 tool calls use the probe paths. "Nine" matches none of these counts. The leak itself is unambiguous.

**m4. The `/work` parenthetical is incomplete.**
> "the only `/work` substrings are inside `crossref.org/works` and `openalex.org/works` URLs." (Section 7.2)

The clean transcript also contains `feynman.is/docs/workflows/review/`, `/deep-research/`, and `/literature-review/` URLs. The substantive claim — zero references to the probe fixtures — holds (0 `eval-scorer-probe` hits).

**m5. "last two months of releases" is ~7 weeks.**
> "for the last two months of releases the eval was either not run or not recorded." (Section 8.4)

0.5.3 (2026-09-24) to 0.5.69 (2026-11-13) is 50 days. Say "the last ~7 weeks" or "since 0.5.3."

**m6. The zero-cost cause is inferred, not verified.**
> "Every committed table reports `$0.00` because the provider entry in `models.json` has no `cost` block." (Section 1)

`models.json` is not in the repository; the committed runs used an external file. The README says cost is 0 when no cost block exists, and all `usage.cost_usd` are 0, so the inference is plausible, but "because" is not directly checkable from the repository. Phrase as "consistent with the documented behavior" or "the committed rows record no cost."

**m7. "Title match is 97–100%" is aggregate.**
> "Title match is 97–100%, with five mismatches across two rows." (Section 1)

The 97% values are means; the underlying rows are 92.3% (baseline q01) and 93.0% (final Opus q10). The "five mismatches" sentence mitigates, but "row-level title match ranges 92–100%; aggregate means 97–100%" would be precise.

**m8. The v0.5.3 release note's 0.5.2 comparison is also inconsistent, and the report does not flag it.**
`RELEASES.md` line 476: "(0.5.2: 9-14 minutes, 43 of 43 citations)". The relevant committed 0.5.2 pre-wait Terra row has 28 citations and 3/4 completion; 43/43 is the 0.5.0 Terra file. The report flags the Markdown summary's "0.5.2 run" pointing at a 0.5.0 file, but not this release-note instance of the same mislabel.

**m9. Appendix B omits the transcripts and `experiments/score-verifier-output.log`.**
The contamination claims rely on transcripts; the inventory lists only the output files. The transcripts exist under `/state/.feynman/sessions/subagent-artifacts/` and the clean one has 0 fixture references, so the claim is true, but the artifact inventory is incomplete.

**m10. Sources [2], [5], [7], [8] are not cited by number in the body.**
They are used in the question table and the verifier fixture, but only [1], [3], [4], [6] appear as bracketed citations. Either map them inline or label them as background.

**m11. "one runtime verification probe" vs. the provenance's "2 runtime verification probes."**
The report explains the contaminated attempt, so this is a wording inconsistency, not a substantive error.

---

## Questions for Authors

1. Section 8.1 still prints 4/4 vs. 2/4 *p* = 0.43; should it be removed, or relabeled as the cross-model Terra-vs-Opus comparison that Section 5.2 now says is invalid?
2. Does the `terra-r2` / `opus-r2` workdir naming indicate an earlier uncommitted round? If so, does "one run per configuration" describe the committed record only?
3. Is the v0.5.3 release note's "0.5.2: 43 of 43" a third instance of the 0.5.0/0.5.2 mislabel?
4. Where is the clean verifier transcript archived, and should it be added to Appendix B?

---

## Verdict

**Verification verdict: pass with major corrections.** The central thesis and nearly all quantitative table rows are supported. Two evidence-integrity issues remain: Section 8.1's statistical table contradicts the corrected Section 5.2, and Strength #3's trace-capture claim is false about workdir deletion. The 08:54:08 edit resolved the q01 re-score omission and the Opus p-value misattribution in Section 5.2. Confidence: high on the table/sum arithmetic and probe outputs; high on the Section 8.1 inconsistency and the trace-capture error.

---

## Revision Plan

1. **Fix M1.** In Section 8.1, remove "4/4 vs. 2/4 *p* = 0.43" or label it as the cross-model Terra-vs-Opus comparison; change "Paired comparisons | partial" to "none for Opus (different question sets); Terra only."

## 3. Strengths: what an eval engineer should copy

These are not consolations. They are the parts of the harness that are genuinely better than the median agent eval.

1. **No LLM judge for the headline metric.** Citation validity and title match are deterministic. This avoids position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases documented for LLM judges [6]. It also makes the scorer cheap to rerun.
2. **Per-question isolation.** Each run gets a fresh temp workspace and its own `FEYNMAN_HOME`, so one question cannot contaminate another through files or config. This is the right default and is exactly what my first verifier probe violated.
3. **Trace capture.** The result row records `git_sha`, `git_dirty`, `feynman_version`, model, the `workdir` path, per-question token usage, and a count of session files. The full session JSONL lives inside the workdir, so the trace is auditable while that directory exists; if it is deleted, the row retains provenance metadata but not the session content.
4. **Failures are retained.** Timed-out and incomplete rows are written to the JSONL and shown in the Markdown table rather than dropped. The baseline's 45-minute q10 timeout is visible, not hidden.
5. **Frozen-set discipline.** The README says: keep the set fixed; if you must change a question, bump the id rather than reuse one. That is the correct rule for longitudinal comparison.
6. **Self-aware caveats.** The README says a single run is noisy, tells the reader to inspect listed failures before calling something a hallucination, and lists the next metric lanes that are not built. This is unusually honest documentation.
7. **Low-cost verifier.** A verification pass on a six-paragraph draft cost 594,620 tokens and $0.0174 on `deepseek-v4.1-flash` in this environment. That is cheap enough to run on every draft, which is the right operating point for a verification layer.

---
33:**What is good.** Feynman ships a real research-quality eval, not a vibes-based demo. It uses deterministic checks against arXiv, Crossref, and doi.org, with no LLM judge. Each question runs in an isolated temp workspace and isolated `FEYNMAN_HOME`, with telemetry off. Every row records the git SHA, dirty flag, Feynman version, model, wall time, token usage, failures, and the workdir containing the full session. Failures are kept in the results rather than deleted. The README states its own limitations ("Treat a single run as noisy"; "read the listed rows before calling something a hallucination"). These are practices many agent evals do not have.
39:**Provenance is weaker than the table suggests.** The headline 0.5.3 runs were made on a **dirty tree** (`git_dirty: true`) at commit `c1e0b29`, whose `package.json` says `0.5.2`; the recorded version field says `0.5.3`. The commit that adds the `bg_wait` rule the summary says was included is a *descendant* of that eval commit. One result file (four rows) references a git SHA (`d926547`) that does not exist in the public repository. The workdirs are local macOS paths under `/Users/advaitpaliwal/...` or `/var/folders/...`, so `--rescore` cannot be reproduced from the repository alone.

## 1. Executive summary

**What is good.** Feynman ships a real research-quality eval, not a vibes-based demo. It uses deterministic checks against arXiv, Crossref, and doi.org, with no LLM judge. Each question runs in an isolated temp workspace and isolated `FEYNMAN_HOME`, with telemetry off. Every row records the git SHA, dirty flag, Feynman version, model, wall time, token usage, failures, and the workdir containing the full session. Failures are kept in the results rather than deleted. The README states its own limitations ("Treat a single run as noisy"; "read the listed rows before calling something a hallucination"). These are practices many agent evals do not have.

**What is measured.** The headline metrics are bibliographic: whether cited arXiv IDs and DOIs resolve, whether the resolved title appears near the identifier, whether expected key papers are present, and whether the final output plus a provenance sidecar exist. They do **not** measure whether the sentence attached to a citation is true. A sentence that says a paper found the *opposite* of its central claim still scores 100% on title match, because the title tokens are present and the negation is invisible to a bag-of-words overlap check.

**What the committed evidence shows.** In all 22 committed rows, citation validity is 100% in every row that has citations, and key-paper recall is 100% in every completed row. The only pass/fail variation is completion, on differing question subsets: 4/4, 3/4, 2/4, 2/2, and one 45-minute timeout. The committed record contains no unresolved citation in a completed row, though q01 lookups in the two pre-wait runs were manually re-scored (see §5.2). Aggregate title match is 97–100%; the underlying row-level values are 92.3% (baseline q01) and 93.0% (final Opus q10), with five mismatches across two rows. In other words, on the public record the eval is primarily a **completion detector** with a bibliographic sanity check, not a research-quality gradient.

**Provenance is weaker than the table suggests.** The headline 0.5.3 runs were made on a **dirty tree** (`git_dirty: true`) at commit `c1e0b29`, whose `package.json` says `0.5.2`; the recorded version field says `0.5.3`. The commit that adds the `bg_wait` rule the summary says was included is a *descendant* of that eval commit. One result file (four rows) references a git SHA (`d926547`) that does not exist in the public repository. The workdirs are local macOS paths under `/Users/advaitpaliwal/...` or `/var/folders/...`, so `--rescore` cannot be reproduced from the repository alone.

**Cadence and statistics are thin.** The last committed eval result is dated 2026-09-24 and scored 0.5.3-era prompts. Since then, 66 release sections (0.5.4–0.5.69) and 10 commits touching `prompts/`, `.feynman/agents/`, `.feynman/SYSTEM.md`, or `skills/` have landed. There is no reference to `evals/` in `.github/workflows/` or in any `package.json` script, so the eval is manual. Each configuration was run once; most on four questions, one on two. A 4/4 versus 3/4 completion difference is not statistically distinguishable (Fisher exact two-sided *p* = 1.0; Wilson 95% CI for 4/4 is [0.51, 1.00]).

**Cost is unmeasured.** Every committed table reports `$0.00`; the rows record no cost. The README documents that cost is 0 when the provider's `models.json` entry has no `cost` block, which is consistent with the rows, but that external `models.json` is not in the repository. Token counts are large and heavy-tailed: 3.34M tokens per question for the 0.5.3 Terra run, 5.48M for the 0.5.3 Opus run, and 18.03M for the baseline's timed-out q10. A failed question consumed 28% of its run's tokens.

**What is good.** Feynman ships a real research-quality eval, not a vibes-based demo. It uses deterministic checks against arXiv, Crossref, and doi.org, with no LLM judge. Each question runs in an isolated temp workspace and isolated `FEYNMAN_HOME`, with telemetry off. Every row records the git SHA, dirty flag, Feynman version, model, wall time, token usage, failures, and the workdir containing the full session. Failures are kept in the results rather than deleted. **What is measured.** The headline metrics are bibliographic: whether cited arXiv IDs and DOIs resolve, whether the resolved title appears near the identifier, whether expected key papers are present, and whether the final output plus a provenance sidecar exist. They do **not** measure whether the sentence attached to a citation is true. A sentence that says a paper found the *opposite* of its central claim still scores 100% on title match, because the title tokens are present and the negation is invisible to a bag-of-words overlap check.

**What the committed evidence shows.** In all 22 committed rows, citation validity is 100% in every row that has citations, and key-paper recall is 100% in every completed row. The only pass/fail variation is completion, on differing question subsets: 4/4, 3/4, 2/4, 2/2, and one 45-minute timeout. The committed record contains no unresolved citation in a completed row, though q01 lookups in the two pre-wait runs were manually re-scored (see §5.2). Aggregate title match is 97–100%; the underlying row-level values are 92.3% (baseline q01) and 93.0% (final Opus q10), with five mismatches across two rows. That run is **not** a capability measurement; it is a demonstration of fixture leakage. It also shows why the harness's own per-question isolation matters: an eval that leaves its answer key or probe fixtures in the agent's workspace measures the agent's ability to find the answer key. The clean rerun is the one reported above.

A second contamination channel is model-level: the 12 questions and their expected key papers are public in the repository, and most key papers are famous. A model that memorized "Snell 2024 = 2408.03314" can satisfy `key_recall` without retrieval. The eval has no private holdout, no canary, and no post-cutoff question set. This is the classic benchmark-overfitting risk identified by Kapoor et al. [1].

---

## 8. Reliability, contamination, and reporting

### 8.1 Reliability

| Property | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Repeated runs per configuration | none | one row per question per config |
| Confidence intervals | none in results | I computed Wilson CI for 4/4: [0.51, 1.00] |
| Paired comparisons | partial | Terra has the same four questions; the Opus final run changed the subset (biology refused) |
| Statistical test | none | 4/4 vs. 3/4 Fisher *p* = 1.0 (Terra, like-for-like); the Opus arm changes the question subset, so it is not tested |
| Model variance | none | one model per run; all agents inherit it |
| Prompt/runtime ablation | confounded | prompt changes ship with Pi/runtime updates in the same releases |
| Timeout sensitivity | high | one 45-minute timeout; 18M tokens |
| Cost variance | unmeasured | `$0.00` in every table |

The eval is a **single-shot smoke test**. That is a legitimate design for a pre-release check, but it is not enough to support "0.5.3 is better than 0.5.2" or "100% citation validity" as stable properties.
